title: NASA reports suspension of COVE surface radiation validation site
excerpt: The Chesapeake Light Station site, which operated from 2000 to 2016, has been indefinitely suspended due to structural concerns.
bodyHtml:
NASA announced on October 30, 2026, that the legacy CERES Ocean Validation Experiment (COVE) site at Chesapeake Light Station has been indefinitely suspended. The site, which provided surface radiation measurements, ceased operations after 17 years of continuous activity.

The COVE site was located 25km from the closest land point in Virginia Beach. It was one of the sites belonging to the Baseline Surface Radiation Network, which serves as a standard for surface radiation measurements.

NASA maintains two other active sites for the CERES Radiation Validation Experiment at Granite Island, Michigan, and NASA Langley in Hampton, Virginia. The Granite Island site was established in the summer of 2018, located 19 km due North of Marquette, Michigan, and 10 km to the closest land point. The site at NASA Langley was established in December 2014.

The active sites are two of only 43 Baseline Surface Radiation Network sites operational in the world.
